newsitem.title: GERMANY: KJS may hold back on planned coffee price rise.
newsitem.headline: KJS may hold back on planned coffee price rise.

text.p: Kraft Jacobs Suchard (KJS), the leading German coffee roaster, said it may hold back on a third retail price rise initially announced for early June should green coffee prices fall.
"We don't want another price hike and if we can avoid it, we will do so," KJS chairman Germany, Bernhard Huber, told the company's annual news conference.
"But we don't expect an easing of the tight supply scenario in quality coffees over the next few months."
"After all, we're only now moving into the Brazilian winter season, which could bring damaging frosts between June and August and cause further price explosions."

KJS, which is part of the Philip Morris Cos Inc group, said the next increase would probably add one mark to earlier price rises of a combined 2.50 marks per 500 grams packet of roasted coffee, which were copied by the majority of competitors.
At the beginning of May KJS had been contemplating raising prices of its "Jacobs" range of coffee products by 1.50 or 2.00 marks in June, which would be the third increase this year.
Huber said average prices on German supermarket shelves were only now approaching the psychological 10-mark barrier, compared with 6.78 marks in January.
Roasters were worried that if prices reached 12 marks or more, consumption could fall sharply.
Their French counterparts had been successful in implementing three or four price increases and in some Scandinavian markets prices had already gone up six times this year.
The company, which improved its market share to 31.5 percent at the end of April compared with 28.5 percent in 1996, described its coffee operations as "profitable", but would not elaborate.
KJS coffee sales in 1996 dropped by 7.7 percent to 2.2 billion marks, accounting for the largest single share of total group sales of 4.3 billion marks (4.3 billion 1995).
These also include chocolate sold by Suchard and a wide range of food products from the Kraft product range.
